pages.title: Pressure as a function of rate
pages.text:
Pressure as a function of rate
With ﬁxed stroke volume,
Q = HV s/1000.
With one downstream resistance,
P = Pv + RQ = Pv + aH, a = RVs/1000.
H is in beats/min and Q is in L/min.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 2 / 18

pages.title: The initial pressure
pages.text:
The initial pressure
Vs = 100, P v = 5, R = 15, H = 60.
Q = 6 L/min, P = 5 + 15(6) = 95 mmHg .
The equation describes a mean pressure; it contains no pulse or storage state.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 3 / 18

pages.title: A resistance disturbance
pages.text:
A resistance disturbance
Hold H = 60 and let R fall from 15 to 10.
P = 5 + 10(6) = 65 mmHg .
For a 95 mmHg target,
P∗ − P = 30 mmHg.
This error is the input to the next correction.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 4 / 18

pages.title: A measured error changes the next rate
pages.text:
A measured error changes the next rate
Hn+1 = Hn + k(P∗ − Pn), P n = Pv + aHn.
Use k = 0.5 once every ten seconds.
H1 = 60 + 0 .5(95 − 65) = 75 beats /min.
Then P1 = 5 + 75 = 80 mmHg .
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 6 / 18

pages.title: Find the equilibrium first
pages.text:
Find the equilibrium ﬁrst
At equilibrium, Hn+1 = Hn = H∗.
0 = k(P∗ − Pv − aH∗).
For k ̸= 0 and a > 0,
H∗ = (P∗ − Pv)/a.
Here H∗ = 90 beats/min.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 8 / 18

pages.title: Subtract the equilibrium
pages.text:
Subtract the equilibrium
Put en = Hn − H∗. Since P∗ − Pv = aH∗,
en+1 = en − kaen.
Thus
en+1 = (1 − ka)en , e n = (1 − ka)ne0.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 9 / 18

pages.title: Read stability from one multiplier
pages.text:
Read stability from one multiplier
Let r = 1 − ka.
en = rne0.
0 < ka < 1 same-sign shrinking errors
ka = 1 one-step correction
1 < ka < 2 alternating shrinking errors
ka = 2 persistent alternation
Convergence requires |r| < 1.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 10 / 18

pages.title: The rate cannot increase without bound
pages.text:
The rate cannot increase without bound
The implementation clips the proposed rate to [40, 160].
At R = 4,
H∗ = (95 − 5)/0.4 = 225 > 160.
At the upper bound,
P = 5 + 0 .4(160) = 69 mmHg .
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 13 / 18

pages.title: Why more gain does not solve this case
pages.text:
Why more gain does not solve this case
The largest available ﬂow is
Qmax = 160(100)/1000 = 16 L /min.
The largest available pressure is 69 mmHg. The residual error is 95 − 69 = 26 mmHg .
Changing k cannot change this bound.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 14 / 18

pages.title: Physiological feedback mechanisms
pages.text:
Physiological feedback mechanisms
The recurrence has one sensor, one scalar error and one actuator.
A baroreﬂex can alter
vascular and cardiac behavior, including mechanisms absent from P = Pv + aH.
Delays and additional states can change the multiplier calculation.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 15 / 18

pages.title: The weight of a static column
pages.text:
The weight of a static column
A column of depth d and area A has weight ρAdg.
(Pbottom − Ptop)A = ρAdg.
Pbottom − Ptop = ρgd .
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 16 / 18
